newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ATHERTON STILL EAGER FOR ENGLAND SUCCESS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ATHERTON STILL EAGER FOR ENGLAND SUCCESS.

text.p: Mike Atherton, England's captain for the tours of Zimbabwe and New Zealand, says it is difficult to keep leading a losing side but his desire to succeed is as strong as ever.
Atherton underlined his determination on the eve of departure for the first leg of his team's 1996-97 assignment, a five-week schedule in Zimbabwe followed by almost two months in New Zealand.
England have yet to win a test series overseas under Atherton, having lost 3-1 in West Indies in early 1994, 3-1 in Australia in 1994-95 and 1-0 in South Africa in 1995-96.
"I feel pretty comfortable with the England job at the moment and refreshed after a break. But, at the same time, it's difficult to keep taking a losing side around," said Atherton.
"We have a new vice-captain now in Nasser Hussain, and others like (Nick) Knight and (John) Crawley are also at the right sort of age and getting a little bit more experience.
"There are so many factors involved but, first of all, I need to keep on enjoying the captaincy and to keep my place in the side.

"I know that if I play all winter then I will have captained England 40 times and I will be close to the record, but I don't feel any need to get that record. Someone else would break it again one day, anyway."
If Atherton keeps the job, he should break former England captain Peter May's 41-test record in next year's Ashes showpiece -- the second test at Lord's in June.

"I'm just looking to improve as a captain, and I feel at present that I am improving,' Atherton said. "I do analyse myself at the end of every Test and I think I react a bit quicker on the field to certain situations.
"But, overall, I believe captaincy is a form thing as much as batting or bowling. Sometimes everything goes right and on other occasions nothing will run for you.
"I'm very happy with the management personnel around me, and my determination to succeed is as great as ever.
"It's nonsense to suggest everything depends on the captain. You need players playing well, and players with drive and determination.
"My desire is there and I think this particular group of players have that desire as well.
"Our record in recent tours has been poor and this time we've tried to get our preparation absolutely right."

One of Atherton's early tasks is to overcome the loss of leading pace bowler Dominic Cork, who has pulled out of the Zimbabwe tour because of marital problems. He is to join the squad for the New Zealand itinerary.
England's skipper must also bring the best out of left-arm spinner Phil Tufnell and paceman Andrew Caddick, two cricketers with whom he has experienced difficulties on previous tours.
